name: Skilled Worker Permit (H1/H2)

requirement_groups.name: H1 -- occupation on Rwanda's skills-demand list

requirements.blocker_text: Occupation appears on Rwanda's skills-demand list.

requirements.fix_path: Secure a job offer from a Rwandan employer.

outcome.duration_length: H1: up to 3 years; H2: up to 2 years

sources.title: Directorate General of Immigration and Emigration (DGIE), Rwanda -- employment permits: H1 (demand-list occupations, 3yr, 150,000 RWF), H2 (general employer-sponsored, 2yr, 150,000 RWF); related categories E1 (government/parastatal, 2yr), E2 (bilateral technical assistance, 2yr), H3 (journalists, 2yr), H4 (regional semi-skilled, 2yr, 50,000 RWF), H5 (international organizations, 2yr), H6 (reciprocal agreements), N2 (NGO employees, 2yr), J (refugees with a Rwandan job offer, 2yr), Q1 (intra-company transfer, 1yr), Q2 (short-term assignment, 1yr, 250,000 RWF), R (special pass, employment under 90 days, 3mo, 50,000 RWF)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Rwanda). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- fully tier-1 DGIE sourced, and unusually granular: Rwanda operates AT LEAST 11 distinct employment-permit letter categories (H1-H6, E1-E2, N2, J, Q1-Q2, R), far more finely segmented than most countries in this dataset's work-permit systems -- only H1/H2 (the two general skilled-worker tracks) are modeled here as the primary route; the remaining categories are listed in the source citation for reference but not built as separate files, a scope decision given how narrow several of them are (e.g. R is capped at 90 days, J is specifically for refugees who separately hold status in another country). pr_after_months (120) and citizenship_after_months (180) are inferred from the L1 permanent-residence 10-year threshold (see rw_permanent_residence.json) plus the naturalisation law's 15-year 'residence' ground (see rw_citizenship_naturalisation.json) -- Rwanda's overall timeline to citizenship via ordinary work-based residence is notably LONG compared to most other countries in this dataset.
